When someone edits an issue title, the write path starts in `src/actions/issues/update-issue.ts`: `updateIssueAction` validates the input, then calls `updateIssue` in `src/server/services/issue-service.ts`. That service checks the actor’s organization scope and permissions, reads the current issue, updates it through `issueRepo.updateIssue`, then awaits `emit("issue.updated", ...)`.

The event bus in `src/lib/event-bus.ts` delivers the event to subscribers and waits for them to settle. At server startup, `src/instrumentation.ts` calls `register()`; `src/server/services/event-registry.ts` then calls `registerSearchListeners()` in `src/server/services/search-service.ts`. Its `issue.updated` handler rereads the saved issue by ID and calls `indexIssue`. That function upserts one search document. Because the update service awaits event delivery, indexing is part of the normal write path and finishes before that service returns. A subscriber failure is reported by the event bus rather than rethrown, though, so a write can still succeed without a fresh index entry.

The searchable copy is the `search_index` table, defined in `src/server/db/schema/webhooks.ts` and created by the migration in `src/server/db/migrate.ts`. Each row stores the organization ID, subject kind (`issue`, `comment`, or `project`), subject ID, optional project ID, searchable `content`, and `indexed_at`. For an issue, `indexIssue` combines the title and description with a newline. `upsertSearchDocument` in `src/server/repositories/search-repository.ts` updates the existing row for the same organization, kind, and subject, or inserts one if none exists. The repository’s lookup is an organization-scoped substring match over `content`; it also applies kind and optional project filters, sorts by most recently indexed, and paginates. `src/server/jobs/search-reindex-job.ts` provides a per-organization rebuild for projects, issues, and comments if the index needs repair.

On the search side, the Ctrl+K overlay in `src/components/domain/search/search-dialog.tsx` debounces typing, parses the query with `parseSearchQuery` in `src/components/domain/search/query-syntax.ts`, then calls its `onSearch` handler with the free-text query and any recognized kind or project filters. The server action path is `searchAction` in `src/actions/search/search.ts`: `withAction` validates against `searchQuerySchema` in `src/schemas/search.ts`, checks organization-read permission, and narrows requested kinds to issues when `advanced_search` is off. It then calls `search` in `src/server/services/search-service.ts`, which checks tenant scope and issue-read permission, applies the organization’s search rate limit, checks the feature flag, and calls `searchDocuments`. Results are mapped to `SearchHit` values with a title, contextual snippet, and link; the dialog displays them through `SearchResults` in `src/components/domain/search/search-results.tsx`. The JSON route in `src/app/api/search/route.ts` is another entry point with similar access, feature, and schema checks.

A query can be refused even when its text looks valid. The schema rejects empty queries, queries over 200 characters, and invalid kinds. Search also fails when the actor lacks organization or issue read access, the query rate limit is exhausted, or the command palette is disabled on the JSON route. In addition, `search` rejects any query containing a colon when `advanced_search` is off, with “Field-scoped search is not included in this plan.” The client parser treats the whole string as literal text when that flag is off, so a colon-containing title can look like an ordinary search in the UI but still be refused by the service.
